title: Distributed key-value store
prompt: Design a distributed key-value store with get(key) and put(key, value) that stays available when machines fail, scales to petabytes, and lets callers tune consistency.

requirements: Functional: get, put and delete for keys up to ~1 KB and values up to ~1 MB; optional TTL.
Non-functional: single-digit ms p99 inside a region, horizontal scaling, survives node and rack failures, tunable consistency.
estimation: 1 PB of data ÷ ~4 TB usable per node × replication factor 3 ≈ 750 nodes.
1M ops/s across 750 nodes ≈ 1,300 ops/s per node before replication; comfortable for SSD-backed nodes.
api: get(key, consistency=ONE|QUORUM|ALL) → value(s) with version metadata.
put(key, value, context?, consistency) where context carries the version read, for conflict handling.
data: Consistent hashing ring with many virtual nodes per machine: smoother balance and faster rebalancing.
Each key is stored on N replicas (the next N distinct nodes on the ring), placed across racks or zones.
Per node: an LSM tree (write-ahead log + memtable → sorted SSTables, Bloom filters per table, background compaction).
design: Any node can coordinate a request: it hashes the key, sends to the N replicas and waits for W acks (writes) or R responses (reads).
With R + W > N, every read quorum overlaps the latest write quorum, so a read sees the latest acknowledged write in the absence of concurrent writes and sloppy quorum.
Membership and failure detection by gossip; hinted handoff stores writes for a down replica on another node and replays them later.
deepDives: Conflicts: last-write-wins by timestamp is simple but can silently drop concurrent writes; version vectors detect concurrency and return siblings for the client to merge.
Anti-entropy: read repair fixes stale replicas on reads; Merkle trees per key range let replicas find differences by exchanging hashes instead of data.
Deletes need tombstones kept long enough for every replica to see them, or deleted data can return during repair.
bottlenecks: Hot keys: replicate reads, cache at clients, or split a value across keys.
Compaction and garbage collection pauses hurt p99; throttle compaction and route around slow replicas.
Rebalancing when nodes join moves data; stream it with rate limits.
tradeoffs: CAP during partitions: this design favours availability (sloppy quorum, hinted handoff) over linearisability.
Lower R or W = lower latency but staler reads; R = W = QUORUM is the usual balance.
LSM trees favour write throughput; B-trees favour read latency and in-place updates.

rubric.text: Partitioned with consistent hashing and virtual nodes.
Replicated N ways across failure domains.
Explained quorum reads and writes (R + W > N) and the tunable trade-off.
Described a storage engine (LSM or B-tree) and why.
Covered failure detection, hinted handoff and repair.
Handled conflicts with versioning or last-write-wins, stating the cost.
Explained tombstones, compaction and their p99 impact.
Positioned the design on CAP/PACELC with justification.
